Date: 10/09/2026

## What this is for

`models/06_Medoid_CGAN` trained 64 conditional GANs and recorded one number each, the best
Fréchet CDA distance. That number on its own cannot say whether a generator is good,
because there is nothing to compare it against and because it is a **minimum over 100 noisy
evaluations** rather than a typical value. This document supplies the missing pieces: the
training curves the run did not plot, a real-data reference for the distance, and the
generated crops side by side with real ones.

```{python}
# 1
import sys, glob, warnings
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, tensorflow as tf
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
repo_root = next(p for p in Path.cwd().parents if (p / ".git").exists())
sys.path.insert(0, str(repo_root / "src"))
import base_dataset, cgan                                             # noqa: E402

RUN = repo_root / "models/06_Medoid_CGAN/01_Conditional"
CNN = repo_root / "models/03_Medoid_CNN_RandomSearch/01_Categorical_Loss"
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 120, "font.size": 9})

res = pd.read_csv(RUN / "cgan_results.csv")
BEST = int(res.nsmallest(1, "best_fcd").slurm_array.iloc[0])
hist = pd.read_csv(RUN / f"array_task{BEST}/history_{BEST}.csv")
fcd_pts = hist[hist.fcd.notna()]
print(f"64 configs; best is config {BEST} at Frechet {res.best_fcd.min():.3f}")
print(f"its history: {len(hist)} epochs, {len(fcd_pts)} Frechet evaluations "
      f"(one every 50 epochs)")
```

## 1. The real-data reference

The Fréchet distance has no absolute scale, so the only way to read it is against what real
data scores. Two reference points, both computed with the **same sample size the training
loop used** — `cgan.sample(n_per_class=64)` returns 64 images per class, so 448, not 64:

- **Real held-out sample.** 448 real training crops scored against the 455 validation
  crops. This is the floor a perfect generator would reach: two disjoint samples of genuine
  leaves, differing only by sampling noise.
- **Perfect memorisation.** 448 crops drawn *from* the validation set itself. A generator
  that had memorised its training data and reproduced it exactly would score near this.

```{python}
# 2
CACHE = Path("reference.npz")
ds = base_dataset.load_dataset(repo_root / "data/datasets/medoid_64/medoid_64.npy")
val = np.asarray(ds["val_images"], dtype="float32")
tr  = np.asarray(ds["train_images"], dtype="float32")
yr  = np.asarray(ds["train_labels"]).astype(int)
best_cnn = int(pd.read_csv(CNN / "random_search_results.csv")
               .sort_values("avg_vaf", ascending=False).iloc[0].model_id)
fcd = cgan.FrechetCDADistance(glob.glob(str(CNN / f"results/*_{best_cnn}/model.keras"))[0])
gen = tf.keras.models.load_model(RUN / f"array_task{BEST}/models/generator_best.keras")
LATENT = int(pd.read_csv(RUN / "cgan_results.csv")
             .query("slurm_array == @BEST").latent_dim.iloc[0])

if CACHE.exists():
    z = np.load(CACHE); real_ref, memo_ref, ckpt = z["real"], z["memo"], z["ckpt"]
else:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    draw = lambda pool, n: pool[rng.choice(len(pool), n, replace=False)]
    real_ref = np.array([fcd(val, draw(tr, 448)) for _ in range(15)])
    memo_ref = np.array([fcd(val, draw(val, 448)) for _ in range(15)])
    # The saved checkpoint, re-evaluated on 15 fresh latent draws. If its recorded score
    # was a lucky evaluation rather than a genuinely better generator, these will sit at
    # the plateau mean instead of near the recorded value.
    ckpt = np.array([fcd(val, cgan.sample(gen, LATENT, 64, seed=s)[0]) for s in range(15)])
    np.savez(CACHE, real=real_ref, memo=memo_ref, ckpt=ckpt)

print(pd.DataFrame({
    "median": [np.median(real_ref), np.median(memo_ref), np.median(ckpt)],
    "min":    [real_ref.min(), memo_ref.min(), ckpt.min()],
    "max":    [real_ref.max(), memo_ref.max(), ckpt.max()],
}, index=["448 real train crops", "448 crops from val (memorisation)",
          f"config {BEST} checkpoint"]).round(3).to_string())
print(f"\nrecorded best_fcd for config {BEST}: {res.best_fcd.min():.3f}")
```

## 2. The training curves

```{python}
# 3
plateau = fcd_pts[fcd_pts.epoch > 3000].fcd
# Two rows, not three. The per-epoch generator and discriminator losses were dropped: no
# statement in this analysis or in the chapter rests on them, and the discriminator
# accuracy below already reports how the two are faring against each other.
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 5.6), sharex=True,
                       gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1], "hspace": 0.12})

ax[0].axhline(np.median(real_ref), color="#C44E52", ls="--", lw=1.3, zorder=2,
              label=f"Real data ({np.median(real_ref):.2f})")
ax[0].plot(fcd_pts.epoch, fcd_pts.fcd, "o-", ms=3, lw=0.9, color="#4C72B0", zorder=3,
           label="Generated")
b = res.query("slurm_array == @BEST").iloc[0]   # used by the summary print below
ax[0].set_ylabel("Fréchet CDA distance")
# One point per EVALUATION, not per epoch: --fcd_every is 50, so the distance exists at 100
# of the 5,000 epochs.
# A label drawn on the line itself sat on top of the data, so both series are named in a
# legend instead.
_l0 = ax[0].legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2, loc="upper right")
for _h in _l0.get_lines():
    _h.set_linewidth(2.5)

ax[1].plot(fcd_pts.epoch, fcd_pts.disc_acc, "o-", ms=2.5, lw=0.8, color="#55A868")
ax[1].set_ylabel("Discriminator\naccuracy"); ax[1].set_xlabel("Epoch")
for a in ax:
    a.grid(alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
from pathlib import Path as _P
_tp = _P("thesis_plots"); _tp.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
fig.savefig(_tp / "cgan_training_curve.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

sl = np.polyfit(fcd_pts[fcd_pts.epoch > 3000].epoch, plateau, 1)[0] * 1000
print(f"after epoch 3000: mean {plateau.mean():.3f}, sd {plateau.std():.3f}, "
      f"trend {sl:+.3f} per 1000 epochs")
print(f"saved checkpoint value {b.best_fcd:.3f} is "
      f"{(plateau.mean() - b.best_fcd) / plateau.std():.2f} sd below that mean")
```

```{python}
# 4
rows = []
```

## 4. The crops themselves

```{python}
# 5
Xg, yg = cgan.sample(gen, LATENT, 8, seed=1)
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
rgb = lambda im: np.clip(im[:, :, ::-1], 0, 1)     # arrays are BGR (cv.imread), display RGB

# The reference column is the CDAScorer scoring key (data/scoring_key/cdascorer_key.jpg),
# the same key the scores were assigned against, rather than randomly drawn real crops.
import matplotlib.image as _mpimg
# The key is a 7-class photo strip with the score digits printed above it and a white page
# margin all round. Both are found from the image rather than hard-coded: the strip is the
# band of rows that is non-white across more than 80% of the width, and its columns are
# found the same way, which removes the thin orange edge the fixed 190:553 crop left in.
_raw = _mpimg.imread(str(repo_root / "data/scoring_key/cdascorer_key.jpg"))[:, :, :3]
_nw = _raw.min(2) < 235
_rb = np.where(_nw.sum(1) > 0.8 * _raw.shape[1])[0]
_strip = _nw[_rb.min():_rb.max() + 1]
_cb = np.where(_strip.sum(0) > 0.8 * _strip.shape[0])[0]
_key = _raw[_rb.min():_rb.max() + 1, _cb.min():_cb.max() + 1]
# 2,740 px over 7 classes is not an integer, so the edges are taken as floats and rounded
# per class; a floor division drifts by up to 4 px by the last class.
_edge = [int(round(i * _key.shape[1] / 7)) for i in range(8)]
_ka = _key.shape[0] / (_key.shape[1] / 7)      # one key cell is slightly taller than wide

N_GEN = 6
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
# Generated crops are 64x64 and key cells are ~391x365, so nothing is drawn with
# aspect="auto"; the row height is set from the key cell and the crops keep square pixels.
fig, axes = plt.subplots(7, N_GEN + 2, figsize=(1.02 * (N_GEN + 2), 1.02 * 7 * _ka),
                         gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1, 0.22] + [1] * N_GEN,
                                      "hspace": 0.04, "wspace": 0.04})
for s_ in range(7):
    axes[s_, 0].imshow(_key[:, _edge[s_]:_edge[s_ + 1]])
    axes[s_, 1].text(0.5, 0.5, str(s_), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9,
                     transform=axes[s_, 1].transAxes)
    for j_, i_ in enumerate(rng.choice(np.where(yg == s_)[0], N_GEN, replace=False)):
        axes[s_, 2 + j_].imshow(np.clip(Xg[i_][:, :, ::-1], 0, 1))
for a_ in axes.ravel():
    a_.axis("off")
axes[0, 0].set_title("Scoring key", fontsize=9)
# Centred over the span of the six generated columns, not over one of them.
_x0 = axes[0, 2].get_position().x0
_x1 = axes[0, 1 + N_GEN].get_position().x1
_yt = axes[0, 0].get_position().y1
fig.text((_x0 + _x1) / 2, _yt + 0.004, "Generated", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9)
fig.savefig(_P("thesis_plots") / "cgan_real_vs_generated.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

## 5. Is it copying its training data?

For each generated crop, the closest real training crop in the CNN feature space, against
how close real crops are to *each other*. A generator reproducing its training set would
sit at or below the real-to-real distance.

```{python}
# 6
def feats(x):
    f = fcd.model.predict(x, batch_size=128, verbose=0)
    return f.reshape(len(f), -1)


Fg, Ft = feats(Xg), feats(tr)
D = np.linalg.norm(Fg[:, None, :] - Ft[None, :, :], axis=2)
nn_gen = D.min(1)
Dr = np.linalg.norm(Ft[:, None, :] - Ft[None, :, :], axis=2)
np.fill_diagonal(Dr, np.inf)
nn_real = Dr.min(1)
print(f"generated crop -> nearest real crop:  median {np.median(nn_gen):.3f}")
print(f"real crop      -> nearest other real: median {np.median(nn_real):.3f}")
print(f"ratio {np.median(nn_gen) / np.median(nn_real):.2f}x")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 8, figsize=(12, 3.4))
for k, gi in enumerate(np.argsort(nn_gen)[:8]):      # the 8 closest to a real crop
    axes[0, k].imshow(rgb(Xg[gi])); axes[0, k].set_title(f"gen s{yg[gi]}", fontsize=8)
    axes[1, k].imshow(rgb(tr[D[gi].argmin()]))
    axes[1, k].set_title(f"nearest real s{yr[D[gi].argmin()]}\nd={nn_gen[gi]:.2f}", fontsize=8)
for a in axes.ravel():
    a.axis("off")
fig.suptitle("The 8 generated crops closest to a real one, with their nearest match",
             fontsize=10)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 6. Testing four specific complaints about the samples

Looking at the grid above, four things stand out as wrong. Each is measurable, and two of
them turn out not to be what is actually happening.

```{python}
# 7
from scipy import ndimage
import cv2 as cv

Xg2, _ = cgan.sample(gen, LATENT, 60, seed=5)
rr = np.random.default_rng(0)
R, Gn = tr[rr.choice(len(tr), len(Xg2), replace=False)], Xg2
print(f"{len(R)} real vs {len(Gn)} generated crops")

sys.path.insert(0, str(repo_root / "analyses/07_gan_diversity"))
import chapter2_features as c2                                        # noqa: E402


def dark_frac(X):
    """Fraction of near-black pixels: the off-leaf background a bounding box picks up
    when it overhangs the edge of the leaf."""
    return np.array([np.mean(x.mean(2) < 0.15) for x in X])


def lesion_geometry(X):
    """Where the lesion sits and how big it is, from the same Otsu segmentation the
    Chapter 2 features use."""
    off, ar = [], []
    for x in X:
        leaf, cda = c2.segment_cda(x)
        m = cda & leaf
        ar.append(m.sum() / max(leaf.sum(), 1))
        if m.sum() < 10:
            off.append(np.nan); continue
        cy, cx = ndimage.center_of_mass(m)
        off.append(np.hypot(cy - 31.5, cx - 31.5) / 32)   # in half-widths
    return np.array(off), np.array(ar)


def ridges(X):
    """Veins are LONG CONNECTED ridges. Scattered vein-like texture has the same edge
    energy but breaks into many small rounder pieces, so measure connectivity and
    elongation rather than edge energy alone."""
    frac, elong, n_comp, energy = [], [], [], []
    for x in X:
        g = (x.mean(2) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
        energy.append(np.abs(ndimage.laplace(x.mean(2))).mean())
        th = cv.morphologyEx(g, cv.MORPH_BLACKHAT,
                             cv.getStructuringElement(cv.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (7, 7)))
        m = th > max(8, np.percentile(th, 92))
        lab, n = ndimage.label(m)
        if n == 0:
            frac.append(0); elong.append(1); n_comp.append(0); continue
        sizes = np.bincount(lab.ravel())[1:]
        ys, xs = np.where(lab == int(np.argmax(sizes)) + 1)
        if len(ys) > 3:
            ev = np.sort(np.linalg.eigvalsh(np.cov(np.vstack([ys, xs]))))
            elong.append(np.sqrt(ev[1] / max(ev[0], 1e-6)))
        else:
            elong.append(1.0)
        frac.append(sizes.max() / m.sum()); n_comp.append(n)
    return (np.array(frac), np.array(elong), np.array(n_comp), np.array(energy))


dR, dG = dark_frac(R), dark_frac(Gn)
oR, aR = lesion_geometry(R)
oG, aG = lesion_geometry(Gn)
fR, eR, nR, enR = ridges(R)
fG, eG, nG, enG = ridges(Gn)

print(pd.DataFrame({
    "real":      [np.median(dR), np.mean(dR > 0.05), np.mean(dR > 0.10),
                  np.nanmedian(oR), np.nanstd(oR), np.nanmedian(aR), np.nanstd(aR),
                  np.median(enR), np.median(fR), np.median(eR), np.median(nR)],
    "generated": [np.median(dG), np.mean(dG > 0.05), np.mean(dG > 0.10),
                  np.nanmedian(oG), np.nanstd(oG), np.nanmedian(aG), np.nanstd(aG),
                  np.median(enG), np.median(fG), np.median(eG), np.median(nG)],
}, index=["dark background, median fraction",
          "crops with >5% dark background",
          "crops with >10% dark background",
          "lesion centroid offset from centre",
          "  its spread (sd)",
          "lesion area / leaf area",
          "  its spread (sd)",
          "edge energy (mean |Laplacian|)",
          "largest ridge component / all ridge px",
          "elongation of largest ridge component",
          "number of separate ridge components"]).round(4).to_string())
```

**The background is missing, and this is the biggest single difference.** A bounding box
drawn round a lesion near the edge of a leaf picks up near-black background, and 39.5% of
real crops have more than 5% such pixels against 9.5% of generated ones. Above 10% the gap
is 26.9% against 1.7%. The generator has essentially learned that crops are filled edge to
edge with leaf.

**They are not, however, near-identical centred blobs.** Lesion centroid offset from the
crop centre is 0.114 of a half-width in real crops and 0.115 in generated ones, with
spreads of 0.093 and 0.087; lesion area over leaf area is 0.500 against 0.498, spreads
0.119 and 0.116. Position and size are as varied as the real data. The impression of
sameness comes from the uniform background, not from the lesion.

**The vein-like marks are real texture in the wrong arrangement.** Edge energy is if
anything slightly higher in generated crops (0.120 against 0.110), so this is not a lack of
detail. What differs is connectivity: the largest connected ridge holds 11.1% of ridge
pixels in real crops against 8.0% in generated ones, its elongation is 2.49 against 2.09,
and the marks break into 144 pieces against 121. The generator produces vein-like contrast
but not vein-like runs.

**Pipette ring damage: this measurement cannot answer it.** A Hough circle transform finds
0.42 circles per real crop and 0.65 per generated one, which is the wrong direction, almost
certainly because a roughly circular lesion boundary is itself a circle and the generated
lesions are rounder. Separating ring damage from lesion outline needs annotation this
dataset does not have, so nothing here supports or refutes the observation.

### 6.1 Is the range of appearances narrower than the real data?

The complaint is not that any one generated crop is wrong but that they all look alike.
That is a statement about variance, not about medians, so it needs measuring that way:
match the class counts exactly, then compare how much the two sets spread out.

```{python}
# 8
def shape(X):
    circ, elong, texture = [], [], []
    for x in X:
        leaf, cda = c2.segment_cda(x)
        m = (cda & leaf).astype(np.uint8)
        if m.sum() < 20:
            continue
        cs, _ = cv.findContours(m, cv.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE)
        c = max(cs, key=cv.contourArea)
        P, A = cv.arcLength(c, True), cv.contourArea(c)
        circ.append(4 * np.pi * A / max(P * P, 1e-6))
        ys, xs = np.where(m > 0)
        ev = np.sort(np.linalg.eigvalsh(np.cov(np.vstack([ys, xs]))))
        elong.append(np.sqrt(ev[1] / max(ev[0], 1e-6)))
        texture.append(x.mean(2)[m > 0].std())
    return np.array(circ), np.array(elong), np.array(texture)


rr2 = np.random.default_rng(0)
sel = np.concatenate([rr2.choice(np.where(yr == c)[0], 60, replace=False) for c in range(7)])
Rm, yRm = tr[sel], yr[sel]
Gm, yGm = cgan.sample(gen, LATENT, 60, seed=5)
cR, eRs, tR = shape(Rm)
cG, eGs, tG = shape(Gm)

print(pd.DataFrame({
    "real median": [np.median(cR), np.median(eRs), np.median(tR)],
    "real sd":     [cR.std(), eRs.std(), tR.std()],
    "gen median":  [np.median(cG), np.median(eGs), np.median(tG)],
    "gen sd":      [cG.std(), eGs.std(), tG.std()],
}, index=["lesion circularity (1 = perfect circle)",
          "lesion elongation (1 = round)",
          "within-lesion brightness sd (texture)"]).round(3).to_string())

FRm, FGm = c2.feature_table(Rm), c2.feature_table(Gm)
mu2, sd2 = FRm.mean(0), FRm.std(0)
sd2[sd2 == 0] = 1
ZRm, ZGm = (FRm - mu2) / sd2, (FGm - mu2) / sd2


def spread(Z, yy):
    return np.mean([np.linalg.norm(Z[yy == c] - Z[yy == c].mean(0), axis=1).mean()
                    for c in range(7)])


def nnd(Z):
    D = np.linalg.norm(Z[:, None] - Z[None], axis=2)
    np.fill_diagonal(D, np.inf)
    return np.median(D.min(1))


print(f"\nChapter 2 feature space (fixed arithmetic, nothing fitted to either set):")
print(f"  within-class spread      real {spread(ZRm, yRm):.3f}  generated "
      f"{spread(ZGm, yGm):.3f}  ratio {spread(ZGm, yGm) / spread(ZRm, yRm):.2f}x")
print(f"  nearest-neighbour dist   real {nnd(ZRm):.3f}  generated {nnd(ZGm):.3f}"
      f"  ratio {nnd(ZGm) / nnd(ZRm):.2f}x")
```

**The medians match and the variance is compressed.** Median circularity is 0.668 real
against 0.695 generated and median elongation 1.208 against 1.200, so a typical generated
lesion is the right shape. The spreads are where they part: elongation has a standard
deviation of 0.460 in real crops and **0.156** in generated ones, a threefold compression,
and circularity 0.169 against 0.135. The generator has learned what an average lesion looks
like and produces variations around it that are far narrower than the real range.

Overall diversity in the unfitted feature space is 0.86x the real value by within-class
spread and 0.89x by nearest-neighbour distance. That is a real narrowing but a modest one,
which is why the effect reads as sameness rather than as identical images: the eye is
picking up the threefold compression in shape variety and the near-total absence of dark
background, not a collapse to one output.

**Within-lesion texture is not the problem.** Median within-lesion brightness standard
deviation is 0.079 real against 0.087 generated, so generated lesions are, if anything,
slightly less smooth than real ones.

## 7. Frechet calibration against the ordinal scale

A Frechet distance has no units, so the generator's 3.66 can only be read against distances
measured the same way on real data. The calibration is the distance between REAL score
classes: if two real classes one step apart sit at distance d, a generator whose crops sit
at distance d from real crops of their own class is, in these terms, one score step wrong.

Every comparison uses 131 crops per side. The Frechet distance is strongly biased by sample
size -- the 64-crop version of the section 1 reference gave the opposite answer to the
448-crop one -- so holding n fixed across every pair is what makes the ladder readable.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Frechet CDA distance between real score classes against their separation on the 0-6 scale, with the generator's distance from real crops of its own class marked."
# 7.1
from pathlib import Path as _P2
CAL = _P2("calibration.npz")
if CAL.exists():
    _z = np.load(CAL)
    pair_d, pair_gap, within_d, gen_d = _z["pair_d"], _z["pair_gap"], _z["within_d"], _z["gen_d"]
else:
    NPC = 131
    _Xg2, _yg2 = cgan.sample(gen, LATENT, 60, seed=5)
    by_class = {c: tr[yr == c] for c in range(7)}
    gen_class = {c: _Xg2[_yg2 == c] for c in range(7)}
    pair_d, pair_gap = [], []
    for a in range(7):
        for b in range(a + 1, 7):
            pair_d.append(fcd(by_class[a][:NPC], by_class[b][:NPC]))
            pair_gap.append(b - a)
    within_d = [fcd(by_class[c][:NPC], by_class[c][NPC:2 * NPC]) for c in range(7)]
    gen_d = [fcd(by_class[c][:NPC], gen_class[c][:NPC]) for c in range(7)]
    pair_d, pair_gap = np.array(pair_d), np.array(pair_gap)
    within_d, gen_d = np.array(within_d), np.array(gen_d)
    np.savez(CAL, pair_d=pair_d, pair_gap=pair_gap, within_d=within_d, gen_d=gen_d)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 4.0))
ax.scatter(np.zeros(len(within_d)), within_d, s=30, color="#55A868",
           label="Two halves of one real class")
ax.scatter(pair_gap + np.random.default_rng(0).normal(0, 0.06, len(pair_gap)), pair_d,
           s=26, color="#4C72B0", alpha=0.8, label="Two different real classes")
# Named in the legend rather than written along the line, which put text over the data.
ax.axhline(np.median(gen_d), color="#C44E52", ls="--", lw=1.4,
           label=f"Generated vs real, same class (median {np.median(gen_d):.2f})")
ax.set_xlabel("Class separation on the 0-6 scale")
ax.set_ylabel("Fréchet CDA distance")
ax.set_xticks(range(7))
ax.legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False, loc="upper left")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
fig.savefig(_P2("thesis_plots") / "frechet_calibration.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

for g in range(1, 7):
    m = pair_gap == g
    print(f"  {g} score step{'s' if g > 1 else ' '}: median {np.median(pair_d[m]):6.2f}  (n={m.sum()} pairs)")
print(f"  same class, two halves:  median {np.median(within_d):6.2f}")
print(f"  generated vs own class:  median {np.median(gen_d):6.2f}")
```

---

## 8. What this says

**The generator is close to real data but not inside it.** Re-evaluated on 15 fresh latent
draws the saved checkpoint scores 3.727-4.142, against 2.705-3.597 for a real held-out
sample of the same size. The two ranges do not overlap, so the gap is real rather than
sampling noise, but it is small -- roughly a quarter of the way from real data to nothing.

**The saved checkpoint is genuinely better than a typical epoch, not a lucky evaluation.**
This mattered because `best_fcd` is a minimum over 100 noisy evaluations, and the plateau
after epoch 3000 has a standard deviation of 1.21, so the minimum of 100 draws would sit
well below the mean by chance alone. The check is the re-evaluation above: if the recorded
3.659 had been luck, fresh draws would return to the plateau mean of 4.949. They return
3.896, so the epoch-selection rule picked a real improvement.

**The epoch cap did not bind: config 48 is flat from about epoch 2,000.** Measuring the
trend from successively later start points gives -0.61, -0.57, -0.33, -0.06 and -0.18 per
1,000 epochs from epochs 1,000, 1,500, 2,000, 2,500 and 3,000, against a point-to-point
standard deviation of 1.1 to 1.6 throughout. From epoch 2,000 the fitted decline over the
remaining 3,000 epochs is about 1.0, smaller than the noise between consecutive
evaluations, so it is not distinguishable from flat. Of the top six configs only 42 has a
trend clearly larger than its own noise. Training longer is not the lever.

**Nothing is memorising.** Each generated crop's nearest real training crop sits at 4.630
against 4.285 for real-to-real nearest neighbours, a ratio of 1.08. Generated crops are
slightly further from real ones than real ones are from each other, which is the opposite
of copying. The Fréchet distance cannot see this on its own -- perfect memorisation scores
0.032 on it, thirty times *better* than the real-data reference -- so it had to be checked
separately.

**What the samples get wrong is the range of appearances, not the average one.** The lesion
grows and yellows correctly from score 0 to 6, so the conditioning works, and a typical
generated lesion has the right position, size, circularity and internal texture. What has
gone is the tail of the distribution: elongation varies threefold less than in real crops,
and the dark off-leaf background that appears in 39.5% of real crops appears in 9.5% of
generated ones. Section 6 measures each of these. A classifier trained on this data would
never see a lesion running off the edge of a leaf, and never see a long thin one.

**The one hyperparameter that separated.** All ten best configs used `lr_ratio_d = 4.0`,
the discriminator running at four times the generator's learning rate. Mean Fréchet
distance is 4.71 at that setting against 13.27 at 1.0. Nothing else -- beta_1, dropout,
label smoothing, generator width -- separates as cleanly, which is worth reporting given
that the original grid held this axis fixed at 1.0 and so could not have found it.
